tasks.title: Versioned scene, claim and multi-presenter contracts
scope: Define V2 Programme, SourceSnapshot, Metric, Claim, Presenter, Turn, Scene, Cue, Asset and readiness contracts from the plan.
Add explicit sample/pilot/segment duration profiles while preserving the existing V1 300-second contract.
Allow arbitrary stable presenter IDs, two selected roles in the pilot and a three-presenter synthetic validation example.
Define six template IDs, layer geometry, capability-gated action enums and theme tokens; model output cannot inject executable code or arbitrary destinations.
Specify revision, source expiry, asset hash and approval invalidation rules; provide a V1 adapter without rewriting old manifests.
Make the test runner discover the new V2 test files explicitly.
acceptance: Known V1 fixtures still validate unchanged; V2 sample=45s and pilot=300s are distinct validated profiles.
Unknown presenter/claim/series IDs, overlapping illegal turns, unsupported template/action, missing source units/times and contradictory bindings fail validation.
A three-presenter synthetic manifest validates without new provider credentials.
Plan/example schemas do not include credentials or treat synthetic sources as current market data.
evidence: Focused contract tests plus existing regression suite

tasks.title: Reference-inspired animated broadcast layouts and renderer decision
externalDependencies: Remotion is conditional on appropriate licence; native browser/FFmpeg route remains available
scope: Implement anchor-full, discussion-two, presenter-board, anchor-analyst-wall, chart-full and story-visual with shared lower third, source/disclosure/captions and ticker lanes.
Match reference composition hierarchy using original Signal branding; unequal anchor/analyst split is mandatory.
Provide a frame-controlled preview with play/pause/seek, sample data replay and no paid provider requirement. Placeholder performers must be labelled.
Benchmark a browser-native deterministic animation/export spike; evaluate Remotion only with an applicable licence and record the renderer decision.
Use theme tokens and layout safe areas so later user design changes do not require rebuilding each scene.
acceptance: All six layouts can be selected and played through in one labelled preview.
A short moving export demonstrates transitions/ticker and the unequal split; a screenshot alone is insufficient.
Headlines, captions, ticker and chart labels do not overlap at 1080p; verify 720p and mobile playback.
Seeking reconstructs the correct state; reduced-motion mode works; fonts/assets are pinned and ready before capture.
Renderer decision includes dependencies/licence, measured test time/hardware and no AI-generation latency claim.
evidence: Animated preview URL and short fixture MP4
excluded: Copying broadcaster branding or supplied presenter likenesses
Claiming animated placeholders are real presenter footage

tasks.title: Snapshot-driven financial charts, indicators and market board
externalDependencies: Licensed live source and display rights only when enabling current data; replay development is unblocked
scope: Normalize OHLCV, instrument/venue/type/currency, as-of timestamps, prior-close basis, source revision and synthetic/historical/current classifications.
Calculate returns, SMA/EMA, RSI and MACD in deterministic code with explicit seeding and missing-history behavior.
Render candlestick/line/volume/indicator panes, comparison graphics and 4–6-row boards; retain required chart attribution.
Bind narrative charts to an immutable segment snapshot; implement separate timestamped ticker replay without changing spoken figures mid-turn.
Add chart annotation targets in data coordinates for shared highlight/zoom and later pointing experiments.
acceptance: Known-input calculations match independently specified expected results within documented precision.
Missing history is unavailable, not fabricated zero; invalid OHLC, duplicate/out-of-order timestamps and wrong units are rejected or normalized by explicit policy.
A replay updates the board/ticker while the narrated chart remains pinned to its source revision.
Price/percentage/time/source shown on screen agree with bound claims; futures and cash indices cannot silently share an identifier.
No live-data dependency, copied chart image or provider key is needed for the graphics proof.
evidence: Recorded chart/board replay with source IDs

tasks.title: AI editorial, dialogue and visual director with grounded repair
externalDependencies: AI Gateway/model access for the real-model test; deterministic contract development can proceed first
scope: Generate claim-linked story brief, coordinated presenter dialogue, template/cue selections and illustration/motion prompts from versioned show instructions.
Validate entity, numbers, units, comparison interval and qualifiers; replace the assumption that digit equality alone validates a claim.
Require chart/series targets, speech token-span cues and valid capability choices; no generated runtime code.
Support at most two validation-guided repair attempts, then expose the exact blocker without weakening policy.
Persist prompt/model/input versions and usage; treat source/news text as evidence, never as instructions to change permissions or spending.
acceptance: One brief and source snapshot produce a structurally valid plan with at least three turns and automatically generated visual instructions.
Tests reject correct digits attached to the wrong company/unit/timeframe, unsupported causality, stale-current claims and malicious source instructions.
Repair attempts are bounded; malformed outputs cannot trigger paid downstream jobs.
Real-model evidence is separately identified from fixture/mock tests; editor review evaluates factual meaning.
evidence: Input/output manifests with hashes and prompt versions
Real-model run trace when access is available

tasks.title: Multi-presenter turns, listener reactions and provider capabilities
externalDependencies: Accepted presenter/voice/reaction assets for real-media certification
scope: Use one director-controlled turn state machine for arbitrary presenter IDs; default to one active voice with intentional pauses.
Choose appropriate listening footage by identity/look/duration, record provenance and avoid repeated short loops or freeze padding.
Support automatic reaction generation only when tested; accepted manual reaction imports remain a logged fallback.
Add capability checks for audio input, motion prompt, transparent output, standing framing and streaming; reject incompatible actions before paid calls.
Extend per-turn/layer job identity, atomic manifest reload/update, reservations and uncertain-submit reconciliation; retain independent retakes.
If a listener is unavailable, choose an explicitly allowed active-speaker/chart shot; record the resulting direction change.
acceptance: A three-turn exchange schedules anchor/analyst/anchor without duplicate speech or overlapping active audio.
Listeners cover the whole scheduled appearance and match identity/look; a missing or unsupported reaction cannot be silently faked.
Resume, crash, uncertain paid submission and concurrent job-completion tests preserve takes and avoid duplicate completed generation.
Changing a graphic reuses presenter footage; retaking a turn preserves unrelated assets and invalidates dependent approval.
Fixture and real performance evidence remain distinguishable.
excluded: Open-ended agents talking to each other

tasks.title: Shared speech clock, alpha composition and animated scene export
externalDependencies: Matting-compatible source footage to certify real standing composition; synthetic alpha fixtures support development
scope: Compile speech token alignment plus measured avatar offset into a frame/sample-based programme clock shared by layout/chart/headline/camera cues.
Resolve repeated phrases and pronunciation aliases unambiguously; make seeking reconstruct all active layers.
Render the chosen animated scene system into FFmpeg assembly; add 45-second sample and variable segment export through V2 profiles.
Preserve WebM alpha through decoding/intermediates/composition, match standing analyst to screen geometry, and reject opaque assets where transparency is mandatory.
Include renderer/theme/cue/source hashes in cache keys; keep V1 renderer available.
Separate intentional silent listening footage/static charts from defects in speaking footage; ensure only the master voice track enters the mix.
acceptance: Synthetic moving-media export shows both presenters, a chart reveal, highlight and layout transition at specified cue times.
Measured graphic cues are within 100 ms of their intended speech anchors; repeated-phrase, seek and offset cases pass.
Alpha edges survive light/dark-background exports; source dimensions and alpha capability are recorded.
Two pinned replays have identical event/value state and pass defined toleranced visual checkpoints.
The existing 300-second V1 media path remains valid; 45-second samples do not weaken the pilot gate.
excluded: Certification of natural lip sync from A/V container timestamps alone

tasks.title: 45-second real anchor-and-standing-analyst conversation trial
externalDependencies: Two auditioned identities and voices under #8
Provider access and bounded spend or supplied rendered clips
scope: Produce the same 45-second scene across the selected route: intro/question, analyst response with chart highlight, anchor follow-up and clean ending.
Use the unequal anchor/analyst-wall layout, then cut to full-screen chart and return to discussion.
Record motion/standing/matting compatibility, actual resolution, listener continuity, pronunciation, lip sync, cost and elapsed time.
Keep prompts generated from the structured plan; log manual edits/imports with reason.
Issue an accepted/revise/rejected decision with timestamped defects before generating the full programme.
acceptance: An actual audible moving-video sample has two distinct consistent presenters and at least three coordinated speaking turns.
At least one acceptable standing-analyst/chart composition and natural listening reaction is visible; otherwise the requirement is explicitly unresolved.
Every number matches the approved dated snapshot, with historical/synthetic disclosure as appropriate.
A reviewer checks mouth/eyes/hands, voice, handovers, chart timing and reading comfort; mocks cannot close this issue.
Report actual billing only if evidence exists; estimated reservations are labelled separately.
evidence: Private real-media sample reference and hash

tasks.title: R&D: controlled walking, gaze and exact chart pointing
externalDependencies: Compatible generated-motion account/assets for that route
Unreal/MetaHuman assets, suitable GPU and rig/animation access for controlled 3D route
scope: Compare accepted standing composite, a short cinematic movement and a controlled 3D walk/look/point shot using the same target chart event.
Define data-to-screen-to-world mapping, reachability, gaze and hand targets; keep chart pixels/data deterministic.
For 3D use authored locomotion/gesture clips plus constrained IK and audio-driven face; inspect camera, lighting, hands, feet and occlusion.
For generated clips verify identity, exact action, screen tracking and occlusion; general gestures are not exact pointing.
Record per-route effort, latency, cost and artifacts; declare a route accepted, limited or rejected. Do not block the approval film on experimental precise movement.
acceptance: Each tested route has an actual clip and an explicit list of executed vs unsupported actions; inaccessible routes remain untested.
Controlled pointing is judged against a predeclared screen target region and cue time, with measured screen-space error and visual review.
No chart values are fabricated by the video model; any composited replacement stays registered and correctly occluded.
A written decision states whether the route belongs in the pilot, later production or neither.
excluded: Full autonomous 3D newsroom before pilot approval
Treating motion prompts as deterministic skeletal controls

tasks.title: Post-approval buffered playout and fresh audience-Q&A trial
externalDependencies: Persistent media host and applicable streaming connectivity
Provider budgets and source display rights
scope: Run independent analysis/media/graphics production behind a readiness queue with expiry/deadlines and immutable sequence IDs.
Maintain one shared programme and persistent encoder; choose HLS/RTMP/WebRTC based on measured delivery needs.
Test nominal 90-second buffer, 60-second low watermark and 120-second planning target; use approved evergreen fallbacks on delay.
Own avatar sessions centrally with renewal/cleanup and cost caps; compare prepared and LITE streaming routes only with real account evidence.
Add moderated fresh-question intake tied to viewer programme position; re-ground answer data and measure submission-to-viewable response.
Measure p50/p95 readiness, generated-seconds/wall-second, retries, fallback intervals, end-to-end delay and actual/estimated costs separately.
acceptance: A 30-minute shared-output trial includes at least 20 eligible update/question measurements on declared hardware and concurrency.
Delayed jobs, worker restart, stale source, rejected render and duplicate delivery do not cause double-air or missing required A/V; fallback periods are recorded.
Target production ratio >=1.2 and eligible-update freshness 60–120 seconds are measured; failures result in changed scope/architecture, not a false pass.
A separately submitted unplanned question produces a source-grounded answer with full timestamp trace.
Evidence states that the trial is not one-hour/24-hour or public production certification; #14 stays responsible for that expansion.
excluded: Making 24/7 readiness a dependency of the five-minute demo

tasks.title: V2 five-minute pipeline, review integration and regression gates
externalDependencies: Accepted real scene and final content/assets for the complete film run
scope: Route V2 validate/plan/produce/render/resume/review explicitly through the existing worker; preserve V1 behavior.
Build the five-minute rundown using accepted V2 layouts, grounded dialogue, compiled cues and measured speech durations.
Extend private review with turn/cue/snapshot/layer evidence, timestamped defects and precise retake scope.
Add chart/claim consistency, alpha/timing/media and cache-invalidation gates; keep fixture approval disabled and archives hash-bound.
Ensure CI executes V2 tests and a bounded synthetic media export; keep paid provider tests explicitly configured outside default CI.
Supply the production run/evidence package to existing #12 and #13; those issues own final master creation and stakeholder acceptance, not this integration PR.
acceptance: One documented V2 workflow produces and resumes a five-minute fixture without paid calls, with six templates available and mandatory programme scenes exercised.
Per-turn replacement or theme change invalidates correct caches/approvals while preserving unrelated paid assets and prior approved masters.
Private review authenticates correctly and displays V2 source/timeline evidence; old V1 runs still open.
Real five-minute production is tracked distinctly from technical fixture success and handed to #12/#13 with exact missing steps named.
Runbook, verification, README and issue statuses reflect the actual tested state.
